hints.title: Dual Capacity Group Profit Obstacle
hints.text: Committing members from a workforce of size n to criminal schemes generates profit. How can tracking combinations across members used and cumulative profit capped at minProfit tally valid schemes modulo 10^9 + 7?

hints.title: Profit Ceiling Clamping Invariant
hints.text: Accumulating profit beyond minProfit satisfies the goal identically to reaching minProfit, allowing the profit dimension to be clamped at minProfit.

hints.title: 2D Backward Knapsack Accumulation Procedure
hints.text: Create a 2D table of dimensions (n + 1) x (minProfit + 1) initialized to 0, setting table[0][0] to 1. For each scheme (g, p), iterate members i backward from n down to g, and profit j backward from minProfit down to 0: add table[i - g][max(0, j - p)] to table[i][j] modulo 10^9 + 7. Sum all table[i][minProfit] values for i from 0 to n modulo 10^9 + 7 and return the result.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates through each crime, scanning 2D table of members N and capped profit P backwards.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recursive branching simulates 2^S subsets which is impossible for S=100.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Clamping profit to minProfit restricts the table size to (N + 1) x (P + 1).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clamping target profit index at minProfit using max(0, j - p).
